sentences.text: Torosaurus was a massive ceratopsian that grew to between 7.5 and 9 meters in length. These individuals weighed approximately 8 metric tons, though estimates range from 6 to 11 metric tons.
The skull of the type specimen measured 2.2 meters, while a larger skull reached 2.35 meters in length.
The name likely comes from the Greek word for 'to perforate,' referring to the window-like holes in its elongated frill.
Othniel Charles Marsh named the genus in 1891.
John Bell Hatcher discovered a pair of skulls with these distinctive frills in southeastern Wyoming that same year.
The type species is based on a partial skull found in the Lance Formation.
A second, larger skull is considered a subadult because it possesses unfused sutures and smooth bone texture.
Analysis of skull fusion suggests that most specimens were very old.
The animal is traditionally placed in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae due to its long frill.
Fossils have been found across the Western Interior of North America, ranging from Saskatchewan to Texas.
It lived during the Maastrichtian age in the region of Laramidia, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
The temporal range could potentially extend back to 69 million years ago.
A 2010 study suggested that Torosaurus might represent the mature growth stage of Triceratops.
However, research from 2011 to 2013 argued that morphological differences prevent them from being the same species.
It is currently debated whether T. utahensis is a distinct genus or a growth stage of a Triceratops species, though this research has not yet been published.
